gap_report_metadata.requirement_title: As a customer, I want to browse available mobile devices, review product details and default configurations, view promotional offers and estimated delivery information, authenticate when required, and seamlessly continue my purchase journey after successful login, so that I can make an informed purchase decision and complete my mobile device purchase successfully.

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: When the Product Details Page is opened, the application shall: Display the default device colour. Display the default storage option. Display the default payment option. Display the correct pricing for the default configuration. Display the estimated delivery date. Display the promotional offer (if available).
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify default device configuration displays correct values for Colour, Storage, and Payment option on Samsung Galaxy A57 5G details page
Verify default device configuration displays correct colour, storage, and payment option on Samsung Galaxy A57 5G PDP
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases validate default colour, storage, payment option, and pricing display. However, estimated delivery date display and promotional offer display are not explicitly validated. This creates a significant gap in verifying customer-facing information critical for purchase decisions, including delivery expectations and promotional incentives.
recommended_test_enhancements: Create test cases to explicitly validate estimated delivery date is displayed on PDP with correct format (e.g., 'Estimated delivery: DD MMM YYYY' or 'Delivery in X-Y business days') and realistic timeframe
Create test cases to validate promotional offer display when available, including offer text, discount amount, and validity period
Create test cases to validate behavior when promotional offer is not available to ensure graceful handling without display errors or broken UI elements
Add validation steps to existing test cases 658 and 668 to verify estimated delivery date and promotional offer display as part of default configuration verification

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: The customer shall be able to: View the Next button. Click the Next button. Continue to the next purchase step. Prevent duplicate submissions when the button is clicked multiple times. Resume the purchase journey after successful authentication.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify Next button is interactable and initiates the next step in purchase journey
Verify Next button initiates the next step in purchase journey
Verify Next button behavior when clicked multiple times rapidly to prevent duplicate submissions
Verify Next button behavior when clicked multiple times rapidly to prevent duplicate submissions
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases validate Next button visibility, clickability, purchase step initiation, and duplicate submission prevention. However, resuming the purchase journey after successful authentication is not explicitly validated. This gap represents a critical user experience issue where authenticated users may lose their purchase context, selected configuration, or progress, leading to cart abandonment and poor customer satisfaction.
recommended_test_enhancements: Create test cases to validate that after successful login, user is redirected back to the exact purchase step where they were interrupted (PDP with selected configuration)
Validate that selected device configuration (colour, storage, payment option) is preserved after authentication flow completion
Validate that user can continue purchase journey seamlessly without re-selecting configuration or repeating previous steps
Validate that session state is maintained across authentication flow, including shopping cart contents and user selections
Add post-authentication validation steps to test cases 659, 669, 664, and 674 to verify purchase journey resumption with preserved context

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: If the customer is not authenticated, the application shall: Display the Login popup after clicking Next. Display Login and Sign Up options. Prevent the purchase journey until authentication is completed. Redirect the customer back to the interrupted purchase step after successful login.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify login or sign-up popup is displayed with correct message and action buttons when unauthenticated user clicks Next
Verify login and sign-up popup displays with correct message and action buttons for unauthenticated user
Verify authentication popup displays correctly and remains stable under timing-sensitive conditions
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases validate login popup display, Login and Sign Up options presence, and popup stability. However, preventing purchase journey continuation until authentication is completed and redirecting back to interrupted purchase step after successful login are not explicitly validated. This gap represents a critical security and user experience concern where unauthenticated users may bypass authentication requirements or authenticated users may lose purchase context, leading to potential security vulnerabilities and poor conversion rates.
recommended_test_enhancements: Create test cases to validate that purchase journey is blocked until user completes authentication with no bypass mechanisms available
Validate that after successful login, user is redirected to the interrupted purchase step with preserved context including selected device and configuration
Validate that after successful signup, user is redirected to the interrupted purchase step with preserved context
Validate that if user closes popup without authenticating, purchase journey remains blocked and Next button re-triggers authentication popup
Create negative test cases to verify that users cannot manipulate URL parameters or browser controls to bypass authentication requirements
Add authentication flow completion and redirection validation steps to test cases 660, 670, and 665

partially_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: The application shall gracefully handle error scenarios including: Network interruption while loading pages. Device unavailability or out-of-stock condition. Slow network response while loading the Product Details Page. HTTP 500/Internal Server Error. API timeout while retrieving product details. Display appropriate error messages without crashing.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify system behavior when user attempts to navigate to All Phones with network interruption
Verify system behavior when All Phones listing page fails to load or displays zero items
Verify system behavior when Samsung Galaxy A57 5G device is not available or out of stock on listing page
Verify error handling when Samsung Galaxy A57 5G device is unavailable or fails to load on listing page
Verify default configuration visibility and accuracy when PDP loads with delayed hydration or async rendering
Verify default configuration visibility and correctness when PDP loads with delayed hydration or slow network
partially_mapped_criteria.gap_analysis: Test cases validate network interruption, device unavailability, out-of-stock conditions, and slow network response handling. However, HTTP 500/Internal Server Error and API timeout scenarios are not explicitly validated. This gap represents a critical reliability and resilience concern where backend service failures or API timeouts may result in application crashes, blank screens, or poor error messaging, leading to customer frustration and loss of trust in the platform.
recommended_test_enhancements: Create test cases to validate HTTP 500/Internal Server Error handling when loading PDP - display user-friendly error message with retry option and fallback guidance
Create test cases to validate API timeout handling while retrieving product details - display timeout message with retry mechanism and estimated wait time
Create test cases to validate graceful degradation when backend services are unavailable, including fallback to cached data or alternative service endpoints
Implement test cases to validate error logging and monitoring for all error scenarios to ensure proper observability and incident response
Create test cases to validate application stability during error conditions - no crashes, blank screens, or unhandled exceptions
Validate that error messages are user-friendly, actionable, and do not expose technical details or sensitive system information

fully_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: The customer shall be able to: Navigate from the StarHub Home page to Mobile → All Phones. View the Mobile Devices listing page. Verify the page heading is displayed correctly. Verify the correct URL is loaded. View all available mobile devices.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify user can successfully navigate to Mobile Devices listing page from StarHub personal homepage
Verify successful navigation to All Phones listing page from StarHub homepage

fully_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: The customer shall be able to: Select Samsung Galaxy A57 5G from the device listing. Navigate to the Product Details Page. Verify the product information. Verify the Product Details Page URL.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify user can select Samsung Galaxy A57 5G device from All Phones listing and navigate to device details page
Verify Samsung Galaxy A57 5G device details page displays when selected from All Phones listing

fully_mapped_criteria.acceptance_criterion: The application shall ensure that the authentication popup: Displays correctly on Desktop. Displays correctly on Tablet. Displays correctly on Mobile. Maintains usability across supported screen resolutions.
mapped_test_case_titles: Verify authentication popup displays correctly and remains functional across different viewport sizes
